# Mobile auth design

**First decision: don't build the identity part.** Use a hosted OIDC provider (Auth0, Cognito, Firebase Auth, Supabase, Clerk) for sign-in, password reset, MFA and social login. The design below is what you configure there, or what you build if you must own it.

## Sign-in
- Use OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE through the system browser (`ASWebAuthenticationSession` on iOS, Custom Tabs on Android), not an embedded WebView and not a password field posting to your API.
- Offer passkeys and Sign in with Apple/Google first; fall back to an email one-time code or link if needed. Skip passwords if you can.
- Each sign-in creates one **session row per device**, which everything else hangs off.

```
sessions(id, user_id, device_name, refresh_hash, prev_refresh_hash,
         rotated_at, created_at, last_used_at, revoked_at)
```

## Tokens

| Token | Format | Lifetime | Stored on the phone |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access | JWT (`sub`, `sid`, `aud`, `exp`), verified statelessly | 10 min | Memory only |
| Refresh | Opaque 256-bit random, only its SHA-256 stored server-side | 60 days idle (sliding), 1 year absolute | Keychain (`AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`) or Keystore-backed storage |

These lifetimes are defaults for an ordinary consumer app; for banking or health, use about 5 minutes for access, hours to days for refresh, and a biometric app lock.

## Refresh
- **Rotate on every use:** `POST /token/refresh` returns a new access and refresh token, and the old refresh token becomes `prev_refresh_hash`.
- **Detect reuse:** an old refresh token presented outside the grace window means theft, so revoke the session and force sign-in.
- **Allow a grace window of about 30 seconds:** inside it, the previous token still works, so a response lost on a flaky network doesn't log the user out. Without it, rotation produces random logouts.
- **Refresh single-flight on the client:** on a 401, one refresh runs, the other requests wait, and each retries once.

## Logout
- `POST /logout` sets `revoked_at` on the session, and the client wipes the Keychain/Keystore entry and unregisters the push token.
- The access token stays valid until it expires, at most 10 minutes. Accept that rather than building a blocklist.
- A password or email change, or "log out everywhere", revokes all of the user's sessions.

## Lost phone
- **Remote revoke:** a "Your devices" screen (`GET /sessions`, `DELETE /sessions/:id`), reachable from web or another device, lists device name and last-used time. Support staff get the same control.
- **Exposure after revoke:** at most 10 minutes of access token, then nothing, because the refresh token is dead server-side.
- **Sensitive actions:** payments, email change and account deletion check the session row in the database and require recent authentication (biometric or re-login within about 5 minutes). This closes the 10-minute gap where it matters.
- **Recovery:** the user must be able to get back in without the phone. Synced passkeys cover this, and so does a verified email plus recovery codes. Never make SMS to the lost phone the only route.

## Skipped
- **Access-token blocklist:** add it only if 10 minutes of exposure is unacceptable for all endpoints.
- **Device-bound tokens (DPoP) and attestation:** add them when you face a real token-theft or bot problem.
